title: KiteBench Sentinel: deterministic load harness, benchmark methodology, and customer sign-off protocol for dedicated capacity throughput guarantees
creator: Ayesha Rao
description: Deliver KiteBench Sentinel: a deterministic, tenant-aware load harness plus a prescriptive benchmarking methodology and customer acceptance protocol to validate dedicated capacity throughput SLAs. The goal is a repeatable kit customers and SREs can run to certify capacity (qps, sustained throughput, tail latency) and autoscaler safety prior to Dedicated handoff.
background: Customers signing up for Dedicated capacity require measurable guarantees for sustained throughput and tail latency that map to their SLA commitments. Existing artifacts are fragmented (multiple harnesses, different ramp profiles, ad-hoc customer runs). KiteBench Sentinel consolidates: 1) a reproducible orchestrator for tenant mixes and KV/prefix cache priming, 2) a standardized set of benchmarks and pass/fail thresholds, and 3) a customer-facing sign-off checklist and runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can reproduce three canonical workload shapes (steady, ramp+burst, microburst) with tenant-mix config files
End-to-end run emits token-level telemetry compatible with Console metrics (latency quantiles, qps, cache hit/miss) to our observability pipeline
Automated pass/fail report correlates percentiles (p50/p95/p99/p999), CPU/GPU utilization, and autoscaler events into a single artifact
Customer sign-off checklist and runbook established with clear remediation steps for common failure modes
Playbook includes safety checks for autoscaler oscillation and graceful capacity fallbacks

testing_plan: Unit tests for workload generators and tenant-mixer
Integration tests to validate KV/prefix cache priming semantics against runtime-1.22 images
Long-duration soak (6 hours) to assert steady-state throughput and autoscaler stability
Fault injection scenarios: network jitter, GPU preemption, controller-delay to validate graceful degradation
Customer acceptance runs with two beta customers using representative tenant mixes
risks: Quantization or kernel changes in runtime-1.22 could shift latency distributions vs historical baselines
Autoscaler policy interactions with burst profiles may produce oscillation if cooldowns are mis-tuned
Customer workloads with pathological prefix diversity may invalidate default priming heuristics
decisions: Use three canonical workload shapes rather than trying to model every customer—provides pragmatic coverage
Emit a single consolidated PDF/JSON acceptance artifact to minimize back-and-forth during customer onboards
Leverage Console metrics ingestion (trace-id correlation) instead of building a parallel telemetry store
tradeoffs: Deterministic tenant-mix increases harness complexity but yields reproducible results for contracts
Tighter failure thresholds reduce false positives but risk blocking customers who have atypical burst patterns
Providing an opinionated default autoscaler profile reduces configuration burden but might not suit all hardware SKUs
implementation_notes: Orchestrator provides YAML tenant profiles: qps weight, prompt-length distribution, cache-priming fraction
Include a 'priming' phase to warm KV/prefix caches and report cache-hit rate baseline
Autoscaler test harness will simulate a sequence: idle -> ramp -> sustain -> burst -> drain to validate both scale-out and scale-in policies
Report generation includes diagnostic attachments: per-tenant latency histograms, GPU-utilization heatmaps, and autoscaler event timeline

customer_onboarding_script: Pre-run: share tenant profile templates and request representative sample logs from customer
Run day: 1) baseline snapshot (15m), 2) priming phase (10m), 3) canonical runs (3 x 30m scenarios), 4) soak (6h) if requested
Post-run: automated report plus SRE-runbook with recommended remediations and re-run criteria
Sign-off: customer accepts report and selects mitigation SLA (retry window, fallback model) to be encoded in contract
